    "id": "ijZkz248ELGz"
   },
   "source": [
    "# **The Till**\n",
    "\n",
    "**Deep Network Development W02/A**\n",
    "\n",
    "**Topic:** Classes, iterators and generators. One shop's trading records, and three objects that have to be written to answer questions about them."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "BO3zxBQUvumr"
   },
   "source": [
    "## **What this is**\n",
    "\n",
    "`inputs.json` holds three records from one shop: the operation log from the till, the minute-by-minute takings across the trading year, and the department catalogue.\n",
    "\n",
    "Each part asks you to write a small class or generator: an object that keeps state and must stay consistent across its methods, an object that does its work once when it is built, and a function that produces values one at a time instead of returning a list.\n",
    "\n",
    "| Part | Write | Points |\n",
    "|---|---|---:|\n",
    "| a | A `Till` that reports the highest subtotal an open basket has reached | 30 |\n",
    "| b | An `IdleIndex` that answers many window queries after one pass | 35 |\n",
    "| c | A generator that walks the nested catalogue | 35 |\n",
    "\n",
    "Each part wants a CSV with columns `id,target`, one integer per row, scored exact-match: `points * (correct rows / total rows)`. Partial credit is real, so submit what you have.\n",
    "\n",
    "**Every amount is in whole pence**, so every answer is an integer. Do not convert to pounds and do not round anything."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "EoKIm9wS38Qr"
   },
   "source": [
    "## **The data**\n",
    "\n",
    "```\n",
    "inputs.json\n",
    "  ops           a list of [kind, amount], the till's operation log\n",
    "  checkpoints   25 operation numbers, for part a\n",
    "  minutes       120,000 integers, takings in each trading minute\n",
    "  windows       30 pairs [first, last], for part b\n",
    "  catalogue     the nested department catalogue\n",
    "  positions     30 positions in the catalogue walk, for part c\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "**The operation log.** `kind` is one of `\"sale\"`, `\"refund\"`, `\"void\"` or `\"settle\"`, and `amount` is in pence and is `0` for voids and settles.\n",
    "\n",
    "A **basket** is the transaction currently open at the till. It starts empty, with a subtotal of 0.\n",
    "\n",
    "- `sale` adds a line to the open basket and increases the subtotal by `amount`.\n",
    "- `refund` adds a line and **decreases** the subtotal by `amount`, so the subtotal can go negative.\n",
    "- `void` removes the most recently added line, whatever it was, and the subtotal returns to what it was before that line. Voiding an empty basket does nothing.\n",
    "- `settle` closes the basket. The next `sale` or `refund` starts a **new** basket from a subtotal of 0. Settling an empty basket does nothing.\n",
    "\n",
    "**The trading year.** `minutes[i]` is how much was taken during minute `i`, in pence. A minute in which nothing was sold holds `0`, and those are the **idle** minutes.\n",
    "\n",
    "**The catalogue.** A list is a department, an integer is the price of an item. Departments contain items and further departments, nested up to five deep. Reading the catalogue means walking it **depth first, left to right**: take each entry in order, and when an entry is a department, read all of it before moving on. Positions are 0-based over the items only, because departments are not things you can buy."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "yrvk0yujtHWU"
   },
   "source": [
    "## **Setup and data**"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "metadata": {
    "id": "rnYEwyfC3MAz"
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "ops:       6000 operations, 25 checkpoints\n",
      "minutes:   120000 minutes, 30 windows\n",
      "catalogue: 876 top-level departments, 30 positions\n",
      "first ops: [['refund', 324], ['refund', 2126], ['sale', 6153], ['sale', 6187]]\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n",
    "# Imports. Standard library only this week. DO NOT MODIFY.\n",
    "# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n",
    "import csv\n",
    "import json\n",
    "from pathlib import Path\n",
    "\n",
    "def write_submission(filename, rows):\n",
    "    \"\"\"Write [(id, target), ...] as a DOCK-ready CSV.\n",
    "\n",
    "    Every part of every exercise this semester ends with a call like this one.\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    with open(filename, \"w\", newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n",
    "        writer = csv.writer(f)\n",
    "        writer.writerow([\"id\", \"target\"])\n",
    "        for row_id, target in rows:\n",
    "            writer.writerow([int(row_id), int(target)])\n",
    "    print(f\"wrote {filename}: {len(rows)} rows\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Download inputs.json from the exercise page on DOCK and put it next to this\n",
    "# notebook (in Colab: drag it into the file browser on the left).\n",
    "_path = Path(\"inputs.json\") if Path(\"inputs.json\").exists() else Path(\"data/inputs.json\")\n",
    "inputs = json.loads(_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n",
    "\n",
    "ops, checkpoints = inputs[\"ops\"], inputs[\"checkpoints\"]\n",
    "minutes, windows = inputs[\"minutes\"], inputs[\"windows\"]\n",
    "catalogue, positions = inputs[\"catalogue\"], inputs[\"positions\"]\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"ops:       {len(ops)} operations, {len(checkpoints)} checkpoints\")\n",
    "print(f\"minutes:   {len(minutes)} minutes, {len(windows)} windows\")\n",
    "print(f\"catalogue: {len(catalogue)} top-level departments, {len(positions)} positions\")\n",
    "print(f\"first ops: {ops[:4]}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "EREA2vmmavEO"
   },
   "source": [
    "---\n",
    "## **Part a: The highest subtotal so far (30 points)**\n",
    "\n",
    "Write a `Till` that processes the operation log one operation at a time.\n",
    "\n",
    "For each checkpoint `c` in `checkpoints`, in the order given, report **the highest subtotal the currently open basket has reached**, after operation number `c` has been processed. Checkpoints are 0-based indices into `ops`, so checkpoint 0 means after the very first operation.\n",
    "\n",
    "The highest subtotal is not the current subtotal. A basket that went up to 4000, then took a refund down to 1500, has a current subtotal of 1500 and a high of 4000. An empty basket has a high of 0.\n",
    "\n",
    "The difficulty is `void`. Removing the line that set the record means the high has to go back to what it was **before** that line, and by then the old value has been overwritten if you only kept one. Whatever you store has to be enough to restore the previous answer, not just to compute the current one.\n",
    "\n",
    "Submission: `part1_submission.csv`, one row per checkpoint, uploaded to part a."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "metadata": {
    "id": "yGY3mUOdirzG"
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "wrote part1_submission.csv: 25 rows\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "[(0, 13672), (1, 11987), (2, 23151), (3, 23831), (4, 13648)]"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 8,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "class Till:\n",
    "    \"\"\"The till's open basket.\"\"\"\n",
    "    def __init__(self):\n",
    "        # Initialize the subtotal to 0, both the previous and current one\n",
    "        self.basket = 0;\n",
    "        self.subtotal = [0, 0]\n",
    "        self.maximum = [0, 0]\n",
    "\n",
    "    def sale(self, amount):\n",
    "        tmp = self.subtotal[0]\n",
    "\n",
    "        # I move the current subtotal into the previous one\n",
    "        self.subtotal[0] = self.subtotal[1]\n",
    "\n",
    "        # I calculate the current subtotal with the previous one + amount\n",
    "        self.subtotal[1] = tmp + amount\n",
    "\n",
    "        # I check if we reached the current maximum subtotal ever\n",
    "        if self.subtotal[1] > self.maximum[1]:\n",
    "            v_tmp = self.maximum[0]\n",
    "\n",
    "            self.maximum[0] = self.maximum[1]\n",
    "            \n",
    "            self.maximum[1] = self.subtotal[1]\n",
    "\n",
    "    def refund(self, amount):\n",
    "        tmp = self.subtotal[0]\n",
    "\n",
    "        # I move the current subtotal into the previous one\n",
    "        self.subtotal[0] = self.subtotal[1]\n",
    "\n",
    "        # I calculate the current subtotal with the previous one + amount\n",
    "        self.subtotal[1] = tmp - amount\n",
    "\n",
    "    def void(self):\n",
    "        # Restore the current value with the older one ( like the transaction has never been executed )\n",
    "        self.maximum[1] = self.maximum[0] # for the max\n",
    "        self.subtotal[1] = self.subtotal[0] # for the subtotal\n",
    "        \n",
    "\n",
    "    def settle(self):\n",
    "        self.basket += 1\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Reset the values I need to keep track\n",
    "        self.maximum[0] = 0\n",
    "        self.maximum[1] = 0\n",
    "        \n",
    "        self.subtotal[0] = 0\n",
    "        self.subtotal[1] = 0\n",
    "\n",
    "    def high(self):\n",
    "        return self.maximum[1]\n",
    "\n",
    "till = Till()\n",
    "part1, wanted = [], {c: i for i, c in enumerate(checkpoints)}\n",
    "for i, (kind, amount) in enumerate(ops):\n",
    "    if kind == \"sale\":\n",
    "        till.sale(amount)\n",
    "    elif kind == \"refund\":\n",
    "        till.refund(amount)\n",
    "    elif kind == \"void\":\n",
    "        till.void()\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        till.settle()\n",
    "    if i in wanted:\n",
    "        part1.append((wanted[i], till.high()))\n",
    "\n",
    "write_submission(\"part1_submission.csv\", part1)\n",
    "part1[:5]"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "eDvnoVtbHOTR"
   },
   "source": [
    "---\n",
    "## **Part b: Idle minutes in a window (35 points)**\n",
    "\n",
    "Write an `IdleIndex` that is built **once** from `minutes`, and then answers any number of window queries without looking at `minutes` again.\n",
    "\n",
    "For each window `[first, last]` in `windows`, in the order given, report **how many minutes between `first` and `last` inclusive took nothing**, that is, how many of them hold `0`. Both ends are included: the window `[10, 12]` covers minutes 10, 11 and 12.\n",
    "\n",
    "The specification is the design. `__init__` is allowed to walk the whole year; every call to the query method afterwards must be a fixed amount of work, no matter how wide the window is. A method that counts zeros inside the window each time it is called does not meet that, even though it gives the right answers.\n",
    "\n",
    "Submission: `part2_submission.csv`, one row per window, uploaded to part b."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "id": "AaagOvUsO3rR"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "class IdleIndex:\n",
    "    \"\"\"Answers 'how many idle minutes in this window' in constant time.\"\"\"\n",
    "    def __init__(self, minutes):\n",
    "        raise NotImplementedError\n",
    "\n",
    "    def idle_between(self, first, last):\n",
    "        \"\"\"How many minutes in [first, last] INCLUSIVE took nothing.\"\"\"\n",
    "        raise NotImplementedError\n",
    "\n",
    "index = IdleIndex(minutes)\n",
    "part2 = [(i, index.idle_between(a, b)) for i, (a, b) in enumerate(windows)]\n",
    "\n",
    "write_submission(\"part2_submission.csv\", part2)\n",
    "part2[:5]"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "Wj6HtUp3ZndJ"
   },
   "source": [
    "---\n",
    "## **Part c: The catalogue running total (35 points)**\n",
    "\n",
    "Write a generator `walk(node)` that produces the prices in the catalogue, depth first and left to right, one at a time.\n",
    "\n",
    "Then, for each position `p` in `positions`, in the order given, report **the total price of items 0 through `p` inclusive** of that walk. Position 0's answer is the price of the first item; position 5's answer is the sum of the first six.\n",
    "\n",
    "Two things make this a generator problem rather than a list problem. The catalogue nests to five levels, so the function has to call itself, and a recursive function that returns a list has to join those lists together at every level. And the positions are known in advance, so one walk answers all thirty queries: there is no reason to restart at the top for each one.\n",
    "\n",
    "Submission: `part3_submission.csv`, one row per position, uploaded to part c."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "id": "w48XNvgv6n8U"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def walk(node):\n",
    "    \"\"\"Yield every price in `node`, depth first, left to right.\n",
    "\n",
    "    A list is a department to descend into. An integer is a price to produce.\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    raise NotImplementedError\n",
    "\n",
    "part3, wanted = [], {p: i for i, p in enumerate(positions)}\n",
    "running = 0\n",
    "for i, price in enumerate(walk(catalogue)):\n",
    "    running += price\n",
    "    if i in wanted:\n",
    "        part3.append((wanted[i], running))\n",
    "\n",
    "write_submission(\"part3_submission.csv\", part3)\n",
    "part3[:5]"
   ]
  },
  {
